MECHANISM: Extreme net positioning by Leveraged Funds in E-mini S&P 500 futures may proxy crowded risk-taking/hedging. If extremes partly reflect forced or constrained positioning rather than information, the subsequent cash-index move can mean-revert after the public COT release; if instead positioning is informed/trend-following, the sign may continue and the contrarian expression should fail.
WHO_PAYS: Potentially leveraged/speculative participants forced to rebalance, cover shorts or unwind crowded longs; this is only a mechanism hypothesis, not an attribution claim.
WHY_PERSIST: Leverage limits, margin/risk constraints and mandate-driven hedging can recur. The effect may nevertheless be fully arbitraged, contaminated by trend exposure, or too delayed because COT positions are measured Tuesday and published later.
OBSERVABLE_TRIGGER: Public CFTC Traders in Financial Futures Futures-Only report for the E-MINI S&P 500 contract, using Leveraged Funds long and short positions relative to total open interest and a release-lag-safe signal date.
CHEAP_DATA_NOW: CFTC publishes annual complete TFF Futures-Only files from 2010 onward and a public reporting dataset. Official variable definitions include Leveraged Money long/short positions and open interest. FRED series SP500 provides daily S&P 500 close history for the most recent ten years.
CHEAP_EXPRESSION: One frozen cross-time percentile/extreme rule on lagged Leveraged-Funds net positioning, entered only after the COT report could have been public, evaluated on a fixed subsequent S&P 500 close-to-close horizon. No contemporaneous Tuesday-to-Friday look-ahead.
WHY_NOT_ARBITRAGED: Not established. COT is widely known and delayed; any simple effect should be expected to be weak. L1 is justified only as a cheap falsification screen because both source routes are public and reproducible.
FATAL_PROBLEM: Publication timing is nontrivial: report dates refer to Tuesday positions, not release time, and 2025 had delayed/backlogged publications during the appropriations lapse. A naïve Tuesday signal would look ahead. The S&P 500 cash close is not an executable futures fill, and positioning extremes are regime-dependent. If a release-safe clock cannot be defined mechanically for the frozen sample, PARK_DATA before economics.
